Understanding Token Optimization for AI

Token optimization is a crucial technique for reducing costs when working with Large Language Models (LLMs). By carefully managing the content sent to AI models, developers can achieve significant cost savings without compromising output quality.

Why Token Optimization Matters

Every interaction with an AI model consumes tokens, which directly translates to cost. When processing large codebases, documentation, or web content, the token count can quickly escalate.

Key Strategies

  • HTML to Markdown conversion — Reduces tokens by 60-90% by stripping DOM noise
  • Code compression — Removes comments, blank lines, and redundant whitespace
  • JSON minification — Eliminates formatting whitespace
  • Smart context selection — Only sends relevant portions of files

Implementation

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized way to implement these optimizations. By creating an MCP server, these tools become available to any compatible AI assistant.


// Example: Token savings calculation
const original = 5000; // tokens
const optimized = 1500; // tokens
const savings = ((original - optimized) / original) * 100;
console.log(`Saved ${savings}% of tokens`);

Results

In our testing, we observed the following token savings:

Content Type Average Savings
HTML documents 75%
Source code 35%
JSON data 30%
